mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS decrease and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies adjust to lower revenue expectations.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between RSAFS decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with high interest rates
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face higher costs.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries benefit from increased demand.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances following a sustained increase in HOUST, or if the correlation between HOUST increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and industrial production (INDPRO) declines by more than 1% in the most recent month, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and INDPRO declines > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of GDPC1 and INDPRO on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
